commit.what: Servex traps: an unlisted tool is reached through call

findings.text: The two most-spawned roles are still told to call tools that are now hidden: `Servex/agents/roles/minion.md:16,19` ("Call the Servex MCP tool `take_worktree()`", `return_worktree`) and `Servex/agents/roles/mastermind.md:17,161` (`create_card`, `card_reply`, `card_set`). None of these are in `Listed.BASE` (`Servex/Listed.js:24`), so a ToolSearch for them finds nothing. Either add a `minion`/`mastermind` entry to `Listed.ROLE` (create_card, card_reply, take_worktree, return_worktree and check_page were all top-10 by calls in tool-collapse.md), or reword those lines as `call({tool: "take_worktree"})`.

`public/framework/ai/doc/tool-collapse.md:3` still opens "Plan only, 2026-10-15. Nothing in Servex was changed". `Listed.js:12` and `Servex/readme.md` point readers there for "history and numbers", so a fresh agent is told the opposite of what is now true. It needs a dated "Built 2026-11-19: Listed.js + call" line at the top, with the BEFORE and AFTER numbers from tool-count.mjs (they are only in session.jsonl now).

`public/framework/ai/doc/agent-context.md:11` still says a mastermind gets the "whole `servex` MCP … + `mcp__local__` item/page twins". After `Agents.js:278` it gets only the listed set plus `mcp__local__item`. The diff touched tools-map.md but not this page.

A fresh agent can't continue from the task folder alone. There is no `requirements.md` (plan.md stands in and quotes the ask, which is fine, but say so). `ask-history.md`, which inbox.jsonl says the minion wrote, does not exist; plan.md says this, but a reader of the inbox won't know. There is no landing/outcome line: the last log line is "Fresh review running", and the commits (02bc1470d8, e4bfc40fb4, 4c970b43b9 on task/mastermind-mcp in worktree qf-1) aren't merged or reported as awaiting merge and a Servex restart.

Errors raised inside a tool reached through `call` are logged as tool `call`. `MCP.dispatch` (`Servex/MCP.js:172`) runs the inner handler directly, so `on_error` in `MCP.call` gets the name "call" and ErrorLine loses which tool failed. Passing `tool` into the error, or having dispatch go through `this.call(tool, …)` after the schema check, would keep the attribution.

There are now two copies of one thing (Law 6). `RemoteMCP.tools()` and `RemoteMCP.catalog()` (`Servex/ext/remote/RemoteMCP.js:458-473`) reimplement `MCP.visible()` and `MCP.catalog()` line for line. The remote `catalog` also returns "Unknown tool" as plain success text, while `MCP.catalog` throws. A shared helper that takes a tool array would remove the duplicate.

A remote `call` to `register_session` is checked against the local registry's schema (`MCP.check` via `servex.mcp.call("call", …)`, `RemoteMCP.js:447`), but the remote door advertises its own override schema (`all_tools`, line 479). This is harmless while the local schema has no `required` fields the override lacks, but the two can drift apart.

`Servex/Listed.test.mjs:124-138` (part 6) fails when Servex isn't running on :8090. That makes the "lean core test" depend on a live process. It would be better as a separate docs-vs-registry check, or skipped with a loud line, so part 1–5 still runs offline.
`diff.patch` doesn't include commit 4c970b43b9 (`Servex/agents/doc/traps.md`), so this review didn't see that change.

`spawn_agent`'s new `parent` text, "Defaults to you", matches the code (`tools.js:439`, `ctx.caller` fallback). The trim from 6.4k to 2.5k with the long form in `Servex/doc/spawn-agent.md` is a clean answer to the ask. The approach is the simplest one: list fewer tools, keep every handler, with `SERVEX_LIST_ALL=1` as the rollback.
